user.title: Source sensors
user.description: Pick the sensors from your inverter and your price integration.

data.export_keeps_vat: I keep the VAT on feed-in income
data.battery_in_use_year: Year the battery was put into use
data.grid_import_energy: Grid import kWh counters (optional, P1 meter)
data.grid_export_energy: Grid export kWh counters (optional, P1 meter)

data_description.battery_discharge_power: Power sensor that is positive while the battery discharges (W or kW).
data_description.grid_import_power: Positive while you take power from the grid.
data_description.grid_export_power: Positive while you feed power into the grid.
data_description.house_load_power: Your household consumption (not including battery charging).
data_description.spot_price: Raw dynamic (spot) price per kWh, without energy tax and fees. The schedule in the next step adds those.
data_description.spot_price_includes_vat: Turn on if the price sensor already includes 21% VAT (the EnergyZero sensors do).
data_description.export_keeps_vat: Leave OFF if you are VAT-registered for the battery: you pass the VAT on feed-in income on to the Belastingdienst. Turn ON if you are a private person without VAT registration.
data_description.battery_in_use_year: Start of the 5-year VAT adjustment period (herzieningsperiode). Private-use VAT is 0 outside it.
data_description.grid_import_energy: Your smart meter's import counters, e.g. tariff 1 and tariff 2. When set, grid import/export and the money use these exact kWh instead of power x time. Leave both empty to use the power sensors.
data_description.grid_export_energy: Your smart meter's export (produced) counters, e.g. tariff 1 and tariff 2.
data_description.price_list_entity: Only needed if you don't use EnergyZero / ANWB Energie: a sensor whose attributes hold today's and tomorrow's spot prices (raw_today/raw_tomorrow, prices or forecast). With EnergyZero installed, prices are fetched automatically. Used for exact price switching and the Predbat price forecasts.

rates.title: Rate schedule
rates.description:
Each period starts on its `from` date and only needs the fields that change; the rest is copied from the period before it. Add future changes as soon as they are announced.

Amounts are **EUR per kWh excluding VAT**:
- `energy_tax`: energiebelasting
- `purchase_fee`: your supplier's inkoopvergoeding per kWh bought
- `feed_in_fee`: terugleverkosten per kWh fed in (a cost)
- `feed_in_credit`: fixed amount your supplier adds per kWh fed in (e.g. Zonneplan +0.02 incl. VAT = 0.016529)
- `vat`: as a fraction, e.g. 0.21
- `net_metering`: true while saldering applies (ends 1 Jan 2027)
- `net_metering_includes_purchase_fee`: true if your supplier also nets the purchase fee
- `feed_in_bonus`: list of bonus rules, each with `percent`, `of` (`market` or `market_plus_credit`), `from`/`until` ('HH:MM', `sunrise` or `sunset`), optional `max_kwh_per_year`, `only_positive` (default true) and `name`. Use `feed_in_bonus: []` to stop a bonus.

Example (Zonneplan from 2027):
```
- from: '2027-01-01'
  energy_tax: 0.08802
  purchase_fee: 0.016529
  feed_in_credit: 0.016529
  net_metering: false
  feed_in_bonus:
    - name: zonnebonus
      percent: 10
      of: market_plus_credit
      from: sunrise
      until: sunset
      max_kwh_per_year: 7500
```
Quote times like '06:00'.

error.counters_pair: Set both import and export counters, or leave both empty.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Already configured. Use Configure to change settings.
